The OK Movement, a political pressure group mobilising grassroots support for a joint presidential ticket of Obi and Kwankwaso of the NDC announced its withdrawal in a statement on Friday.
The group said its national leadership had formally been made to understand that the NDC presidential candidate and the party he represents have decided to discontinue their political relationship with the OK Movement.
In the statement signed by its National Director General, Ughulu, the movement said it in due course, announce its preferred political party and presidential candidate for the 2027 general elections.
But reacting to the announcement, the Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso Media Office in a statement signed by Idris Zekeri late night on Friday, said the claim is both false and absurd.
Zekeri said the suggestion that OK has abandoned Obi and Kwankwaso is, by its very nature, contradictory, adding that it is clearly a contrived narrative by desperate elements intent on sowing discord and generating needless confusion within the political space.
“The Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso Media Office has noted a misleading statement circulating in parts of the media from a group purporting to represent the OK Movement.
“The statement, signed by one John Ughulu, claims that the group has withdrawn its support for Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso and has exited the NDC.
“This claim is both false and absurd. If O.K represents Obi and Kwankwaso (Obedient and Kwankwassiyya) Movements, with each having effective Coordinators, it is illogical for anyone to claim that the organisation has withdrawn support for the two forces visibly advancing the Presidential project of its principal.
“For clarity, the OK political group remains intact, united, determined, and fully mobilised at every level. Its commitment remains firm, and its central objective continues to be the decisive victory of the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket.
“We will not be diverted by cheap propaganda or sponsored falsehoods. We call on the general public, our steadfast supporters, and members of the press to dismiss the purported statement entirely and recognise it as the work of individuals intent on causing mischief.
“Nigerians are fully alert and remain committed to the broader vision: creating a New Nigeria that serves everyone—a New Nigeria that will genuinely be OK,” the statement added.
